source.title: KAPADAGANDA: A Cultural Symbol Of Dongaria Kandhas Of Rayagada District, Odisha
source.inspection: Full five-page extracted text; no interview transcripts inspected.

source_summary.methods: Page 39 reports February 2024 and September 2025 fieldwork: 16 women in Khambesi and eight in Khajuri, using questionnaires, discussion and observation with interpreters. Recruitment was voluntary.
source_summary.leads: Named elders Kudwei Kadraka and Sindhe Wadaka reportedly learned from older women. Colour terms include Kambit, Hinga, Sanja and Kaditi (p. 40).
source_summary.limitations: Age totals conflict with the two elders described as over sixty. Definitions of Ganda vary internally. Historical weaving by women is asserted without equipment records; this needs reconciliation with documented Dom base-cloth suppliers. The 2023 GI claim differs from the certificate date already verified in KB. Claims of inherent slow learning lack demonstrated support. No production ledger, payment evidence or operational cluster record appears.

editorial_decision: Hold new terminology and historical-production claims. Do not equate similarly named speakers across publications. Keep current article and illustrated exports unchanged.
search_result: Targeted searches did not recover a dated operating or delivery record for the proposed local weaving cluster. This is a retrieval limit, not proof of non-operation.
next_action: Resolve historical weaving attribution with a named maker account, loom documentation and dates.
Verify colour vocabulary against speaker-recorded usage; preserve source-specific spellings.
Reopen cluster implementation only with a dated order, commissioning record or delivery evidence.
